kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.acara.cahaya: Buddha's Light at dawn! A rainbow halo rises on the sea of clouds below the Golden Hall; stand on the viewing terrace.
Your shadow stands inside the ring of light. Dao comprehension +1.
The light is as beautiful as ever, but you already received its blessing this week.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.acara.loncen: The Cloud Bell tolls one hundred and eight times; even the mist on the slopes trembles.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.acara.longso: Rockslide! Stones tumble from the cliff; the plank walk and the upper stairs are chained shut.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.acara.ziarah: The Pilgrimage Season begins at %s: long lines of pilgrims climb with incense in hand.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.bela.gou_men: Enough! Enough... Iron Claw yields. No more blows.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.bela.kera_ba: The Old White Ape leaps from the station roof and stands at your side.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.bela.menyera: Gou Tie kneels among the coils of rope. Talk to him to decide his fate.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.bela.sub: Gou Tie and his hunters strike as the new rope is fitted
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.cmd.gagal: test theme lift %s: not possible right now.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.cmd.stasiun: Lower station %s blocks away, upper %s blocks · lower (%s, %s, %s) · upper (%s, %s, %s)
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.cmd.status: %s: phase %s, cabin %s, riders %s/%s, stuck %s, cabin present: %s
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.cmd.ziarah: Pilgrimage: state %s, landings lit %s/9, Blessing left %s days, cooldown %s days, picker points %s
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.gelar.penjag: The cable car is free for life; the Cloud Bell remembers your name.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.herba.habis: That stock is sold out for today.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.herba.nilai: Granny Yao weighs %s in her palm: it is %s years old.
Hold a herb in your main hand to have it appraised.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.herba.pangka: This niche is only for Cliff Pickers of rank %s or higher.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.herba.tali_p: Climbing Rope tied at the waist: your next fall on this town's cliffs will not hurt.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.herba.tali_s: The Climbing Rope catches you! It snaps, but you are safe.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.jaga.datang: Three hooded figures step out of the mist, spirit saws glowing blue in their hands!
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.jaga.kabur: The sawyers flee toward the cliffs. Their footprints are still wet on the planks.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.jaga.ke_pos: Stand at the watch post of the Middle Pylon.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.jaga.malam: The saboteurs come at night. Return to the Middle Pylon after sunset.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.jaga.mulai: You keep watch at the Middle Pylon. The wind whistles through the iron cables...
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.jaga.tangkap: One sawyer is caught alive. Uncle Tie Suo will want a word with him.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.jerat.bukan: A spirit snare pulses faintly. Better not touch it before you know who set it.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.katrol.naik: The keeper turns the crank; the pulley basket rises.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.katrol.turun: The keeper eases the brake; the pulley basket sinks slowly.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.kera.biksu_m: The monks glare at you: killing a monkey on monastery ground. Good Name -3.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.kera.rebut: A monkey snatches %s from your hand and flees to the cliff!
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.kera_putih.m: The Old White Ape points at an empty fruit basket: it asks for %s fruits as a sign of respect.
The mist thickens. Out of it steps a great white ape, old and silent, and it points at the Cliff Pulley.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.kera_putih.p: You tear the fibre from the nest. The Old White Ape screams; from now on it is your enemy.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.kera_putih.s: In a hidden niche among the cliff roots hangs a coil of silver fibre: the Ape Silk Rope.
The Old White Ape accepts your fruit, bows, and hands you the coil of Ape Silk Rope.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.kuli.belum: None of your deliveries have arrived here yet.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.kuli.kosong: Hold the goods you want carried in your main hand.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.kuli.muatan_: Your load tumbles into the gorge! Porters neither fly nor ride.
Load handed over at the delivery room.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.kuli.penuh: The porters already carry 27 of your parcels. Collect the ones that arrived first.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.kuli.sudah_t: %s of your deliveries have arrived here; ask the keeper of the delivery room.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.kuli.titip: A porter straps your goods to his back frame and starts climbing to %s.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.kuli.uang: The porter's fee is 2 NB; you cannot afford it.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.kuli.wadah: The porters do not carry filled containers.
Buy, sell and appraise cliff herbs
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.lift.berjala: The cabin is under way; wait at the station.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.lift.dekati: Go up to the cable car ticket window.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.lift.lanjut: The cable shudders, the wheel turns again: the cabin moves on.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.lift.macet.s: The cabin sways mid-span, high above the gorge
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.lift.macet.t: Uncle Tie Suo shouts from the pylon: "Don't panic! I'm lowering a rope!"
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.lift.naik: The cabin climbs to the Golden Summit. Look at the sea of clouds below.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.lift.petir: Thunderstorm: the cable car waits until the sky calms.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.lift.tali: Grip the rope and climb down slowly; Tie Suo holds you from above.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.lift.terkunc: The cabin door stays locked while moving.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.lift.tiba_at: Arrived at the Upper Station, Golden Summit.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.lift.tiba_ba: Arrived at the Lower Station, Foot Gate.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.lift.turun: The cabin descends to the Foot Gate.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.lift.tutup: The cable car only runs from 05:00 to 18:00.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.lift.uang: The fare up is 1 NB; you cannot afford it.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.palang.tutup: The way is chained shut. Wait until the rain or the rockslide passes.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.upacara: The Cloud Bell tolls, the Buddha's Light appears in the clouds and the new rope shines silver. The cable car is now free for you forever.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.ziarah.batal: Pilgrimage void: you rode the cable car.
Pilgrimage void: you rode a pulley.
Pilgrimage void: the day ended before you arrived.
Pilgrimage void: you left the mountain road.
You stopped the pilgrimage. The Foot Temple is always open to begin again.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.ziarah.dafta: Your name is written in the pilgrims' book. Climb without flying, without the cable car, without pulleys.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.ziarah.jauh: You strayed too far from the pilgrim road; return to the stairs.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.ziarah.kuran: %s landings still wait for your incense.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.ziarah.mulai: Light incense at nine landings and reach the Golden Hall before the day ends
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.ziarah.restu: Summit Blessing: for seven days your meditation at the Golden Hall runs deeper.
The Abbot grants you one Summit Blessing without the climb.
Pilgrimage complete. The next Summit Blessing can be received in %s days.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.ziarah.sedan: You are already on a pilgrimage.
kultivator.kota_tema.gunung.ziarah.sudah: The incense at landing %s already burns.
kultivator.cerita.quest.tema_gunung_tali: Uncle Tie Suo's cable car stalled above the gorge, and the cable did not wear through: it was cut.
The cable car cabin stopped mid-span. Climb down the rope Tie Suo lowers.
Meet Uncle Tie Suo at the Lower Station; he is examining the end of the iron cable.
Lao Dan at the Porters' Post saw something at the Middle Pylon at night. Ask him.
Keep watch one night at the Middle Pylon post (Herb Hall) and face whoever comes with a saw.
One sawyer was caught. Hear his confession with Tie Suo.
The sawyers fled to the cliffs. Ask Tie Suo about their tracks.
Shan Ling the cliff picker knows every niche. Find her on the Cliff Plank Walk.
Release Gou Tie's six spirit snares in the niches of the Cliff Plank Walk.
The Old White Ape is waiting. Ride the Cliff Pulley to its nest and obtain the Ape Silk Rope.
Bring the Ape Silk Rope to Tie Suo at the Lower Station.
Tie Suo is fitting the new rope. Defend the Lower Station from Gou Tie and his hunters.
Abbot Jue Yuan awaits you at the Cloud Monastery to bless the rope.
The new rope is blessed. The first cabin rises carrying Shan Ling, Lao Dan and Tie Suo, who weeps without shame. In this town your name is now spoken together with the rope's.
Abbot Jue Yuan awaits you at the Cloud Monastery. Shan Ling does not come.
The rope is strong, but whenever the wind rubs its fibres Shan Ling looks away. The Old White Ape is never seen on the cliffs again.
Abbot Jue Yuan calls you to the Cloud Monastery. Word is that Shan Ling has left town.
The cable car runs again and your purse is heavy with Gou Tie's gold. Herb prices at the Herb Hall rose by a fifth, and Shan Ling's little house on the cliff stands empty.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_tali_putus: You got down safe? Good, good. Now look at this. Look! Twenty years of iron cable, and the end is as flat as tofu under a knife. That's not wear. That's a saw.
Who would want to ruin your cable car?
Are you sure? Maybe rust inside.
Rust? I've oiled this cable every morning before the dawn bell for twenty years! Rust doesn't leave glittering blue tooth marks. This is a spirit saw. Expensive stuff.

The monks call my car the lazy road, but they've never cut anything but radishes. The merchants? I owe half of them money; nobody kills a man who owes them. Lao Dan at the Porters' Post sleeps the latest. Ask him what he saw.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_tali_lao_d: Tie Suo sent you? Heh. My legs are old but my eyes aren't. Three nights ago I went down for water near the Middle Pylon. A little blue light up on the tower, swaying like a drunk firefly. Fireflies don't saw iron.

To whom? A porter reports, then the porter is told to keep watch, then the porter doesn't sleep, then tomorrow the porter falls down the stairs with two sacks of rice. Porters learn to be quiet. But you're no porter.
A cable half cut isn't cut yet. They have to finish the job. Keep watch at the Middle Pylon post after sunset. If they come, catch one. A man who's caught usually prefers talking to falling.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_tali_cari_: Lao Dan, at the Porters' Post, east of the station. The old man with legs like iron posts. Don't offer him wine; he'll talk until morning.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_tali_jaga_: The Middle Pylon, after sunset. Stand at the watch post at its foot and don't fall asleep. The wind up there sings the cruellest lullabies.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_tali_inter: This boy is crying like a cat dropped down a well. Say it again, loudly, who paid you!

"Gou Tie... Iron Claw. He paid three gold pieces. Said if the cable car falls, the porters must use his men, and the pickers will be too scared to climb, so all the cliff herbs are his." ... You hear that? Herbs! All this for grass!
Who knows the cliffs as well as Gou Tie?
Let the boy go; he's only a tool.
Hmph. You're softer than a monk. Fine, he can carry stones for the monastery for a month. That's scarier than prison.
Who knows the cliffs as well as Gou Tie?
Shan Ling. That picker girl knows every niche and quarrels with every monkey. If Gou Tie is setting something up on the cliffs, she'll know first. Find her on the Cliff Plank Walk.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_tali_jejak: Fled? To the cliffs? Hah, fools. The cliffs are a dead end unless you're a monkey or Shan Ling. Wet footprints, you say? Dew only clings to the boards of the Cliff Plank Walk before dawn.
A herb picker, barely seventeen but with a tongue a hundred years old. She knows every niche. If strangers are on the cliffs, she knows. Ask her.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_tali_shan_: Gou Tie? Of course Gou Tie. Last week he offered me twice the Herb Hall's price if I sold him everything I pick. I said I'd rather sell to the monkeys. Since then the niches have smelled strange.
Why would he want the cable car broken?

If the cable car dies, goods go up on porters' backs, and Gou Tie has a dozen hired porters waiting. If the pickers are scared, the cliffs are empty, and three-hundred-year herbs can only be bought from him. Two birds, one stone.

Spirit snares. Thin qi threads set in the meditation niches; whoever sits there gets their feet tied and falls when they stand. There are six niches on the plank walk. Release them all. I'll come along, but don't expect me to hold your hand over the gorge.
Climbing Ropes are sold at the Herb Hall, right?
Fifteen Spirit Stones, single use, saves your life once. Cowards buy them. Pickers who live long buy them too. Think about it.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_tali_jerat: Six niches on the plank walk, bottom to top. The snares glimmer faintly when you're close. Don't look down. I mean, you can look, just not for long.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_tali_kera_: You saw it? The Old White Ape! My grandmother said it was already old before the Golden Hall was gilded. If it points at the Cliff Pulley, it wants you up at its nest. Ape Silk Rope: fibre from cliff roots spun by the apes for a hundred years. Stronger than iron, and no spirit saw can bite it.
How do I ask for it?
The apes love fruit. Bring ten: sweet berries, glow berries, apples, melon, anything. Don't throw it; set it down near it, then bow. It has better manners than half the merchants at the foot market.
You could try. It'll let go of the fibre if you hurt it badly enough. But these cliffs have a memory, and so do I.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_tali_pasan: Is that... is that Ape Silk Rope? My father said it was a fairy tale for porters' children. Give it, give it, my hands itch!

Look how it drinks the oil... as if it were alive. It takes half a day to fit it to the wheel. And for half a day the station is open like a gutted fish. If Gou Tie is clever, he comes now. Gou Tie isn't clever, but he's greedy, and greed often looks clever.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung.alasan.tal: You are not carrying the Ape Silk Rope.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_tali_pasan: There's blood on this fibre. White ape blood. Hmph. A rope's a rope, and my car must run. But don't tell Shan Ling how you got it.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_tali_bela_: Stay near the station! I can't fit a rope while swinging a wheel key at people's heads. Well, I can, but the rope ends up crooked.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_tali_gou.m: All right, all right! I lost. These cliffs never liked me. Listen, we can talk like traders. Cliff herbs are gold growing on stone, and you know it.
I'm handing you to the monastery. Pay your debt by carrying.
Leave this mountain and never come back.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_tali_gou.t: Carrying? Me? Iron Claw hauling rice sacks for monks?... My grandfather was a porter. He died on the seventh landing with a sack on his back. Maybe... maybe that's why I hate these stairs.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_tali_gou.u: Leave. Hah. Where to? There are a hundred other mountains and a hundred other cliffs. But fine. Next time I'll pick a cliff without monkeys and without people like you.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_tali_gou.s: Six gold bars now, and a share of every herb I sell later. Let me set the prices, let that chatty girl go. Tie Suo gets his car, you get the gold, I get the cliffs. Everybody's happy.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_tali_berka: I've ordered the bell rung, and the monks who always called that car the lazy road are burning incense for it. Funny, isn't it? Sometimes the lazy road carries people too tired to pray right up to the Buddha's feet.
I am ready for the ceremony.

Ride the first cabin with them. When the bell falls silent, look at the clouds. If the light comes, don't bow to it; it's only a polite rainbow. Bow to the people who have carried these stairs for a thousand years.
I will bless the rope. A rope has no sin. But Shan Ling did not come today, and the apes are silent on the cliff. We built a bridge by tearing down someone else's home. Remember how that feels.
I am ready for the ceremony.

Ride the first cabin with them. When the bell falls silent, look at the clouds. If the light comes, don't bow to it; it's only a polite rainbow. Bow to the people who have carried these stairs for a thousand years.
That car will run, so I will bless it. The gold in your purse needs no blessing from me; it is heavy enough on its own. Shan Ling left this morning. She left her basket at the monastery gate.
I am ready for the ceremony.

Ride the first cabin with them. When the bell falls silent, look at the clouds. If the light comes, don't bow to it; it's only a polite rainbow. Bow to the people who have carried these stairs for a thousand years.
The young scholar Pei Wenzhi wants to climb the Thousand Steps for his late mother, but his legs are weaker than his tongue.
Register your pilgrimage at the Foot Temple.
Complete the Pilgrimage of a Thousand Steps: nine landings, then the Golden Hall, without flying.
Return to the Foot Temple and tell Pei Wenzhi about the summit.
Pei Wenzhi lights incense at the Foot Temple and, for the first time, quotes nobody's poem.
His mother always wished to see the Night of Water Lanterns. Bring Pei Wenzhi a Lotus Lantern from the Water Town.
Pei Wenzhi holds the lantern. Listen to him.
That night a lotus lantern drifted on the Release Pond of the Cloud Monastery. The monks pretended not to see the scholar weeping at its edge.
You're a pilgrim too? Hmph. Most people here climb out of fear of hell. I climb out of filial piety, which is of course far nobler. "High mountains know no weariness for a filial son," says the proverb. That proverb has clearly never climbed.
Tired? Me? I was merely... resting at the third landing. Four times. In two days. It is a strategy.

My mother. She wanted to reach the Golden Hall before her eyes clouded over, and I always said next year, because of the state examination. Last year she died, and I passed the examination. Funny, isn't it? Keep me company. I mean, climb too, and later tell me what the summit is like, in case I... rest again.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_pei_daki.m: Register at the monk's desk next door, then climb. No cable car, no flying, no pulleys. Yes, I already asked whether a sedan chair counts. It does not.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_pei_naik.m: Still here? Nine landings, nine sticks of incense. If your legs shake at the seventh landing, that's normal. If you see me asleep at the third landing, that's normal too.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_pei_lenter: A Lotus Lantern, from the Water Town. I know, I know, I said forget it. But if you happen to pass that way...
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_pei_cerita: You made it! Truly? Tell me. No fine words; I'm sick of fine words. What was it like?
Clouds under your feet like a sea of milk, and the roof is gold.
Honestly, my legs hurt and a monkey stole my bun.
A sea of milk... Mother always said clouds were cotton hung out to dry by the sky. She was right and I laughed at her.
She would be glad you tried.
Hah! A monkey! Mother would have laughed until she coughed. She always said even saints must guard their buns.
She would be glad you tried.

Take this incense; I bought it for her and never gave it. Ah, one more thing. Mother always wanted to see the Night of Water Lanterns in the Water Town. If you've ever been there... no, forget it. Thank you.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_pei_lenter: A lotus lantern... from the Water Town, truly? The paper smells like Mother's room. Tonight I'll set it adrift on the Release Pond. You know, I wrote three hundred poems for the state examination and not one for her. Tonight, one.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_pei_sapa.m: Ah, you. I reached the sixth landing yesterday. Without strategic rests. Well, twice.
kultivator.cerita.quest.tema_kuli_sehari: Lao Dan dares you to carry three loads up to the delivery rooms above, without flying and without the cable car.
Carry porter's loads to the delivery room of the Cloud Monastery or the Golden Hall (three times). New loads from Lao Dan.
Return to Lao Dan at the Porters' Post for your wages.
Lao Dan gives you his old porter's staff. Your shoulders ache for three days, and every porter on the stairs now nods to you.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_kuli_tawar: You go up and down the stairs like a young goat. But goats carry nothing. Want to know what being a porter feels like for a day? Three loads, from here to the delivery rooms above. No flying, no cable car.
Because you can't talk to a mountain from above. When you fly, you look at the mountain. When you carry, the mountain looks at you.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_kuli_pikul: Still standing? The delivery rooms are at the Cloud Monastery and the Golden Hall. Dropped your load? Take another; porters don't weep over sacks.
Three loads, and your legs are still attached. Here are your wages, thirty Spirit Stones, a young porter's rate. And this, my old staff. Forty years on the stairs. Now it retires with you.
The mountain monkeys snatch the pilgrims' food and incense. Win back five stolen things.
Make monkeys drop their loot: a light blow, or toss fruit bait on the ground (five times).
Return the things to a pilgrim.
The pilgrims tie their food with string and name the fattest monkey after you.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_kera_tawar: Oh, oh! That monkey took my bun and my incense at once! Incense! What is it going to worship? Child, you look nimble. Those monkeys love to rob people on the upper landings.
On a holy mountain? The monks would chase you all the way to the sea! A light blow, or toss fruit on the ground; a greedy monkey always drops its loot for fruit.
All right, I'll get them back.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_kera_kemba: My bun! A bit bitten, but still my bun. And the incense, and whose sandal is this? Never mind, I'll leave it at the temple. Take this incense. May the monkeys on your road always be full.
kultivator.cerita.quest.tema_rumput_awan: Abbot Jue Yuan needs Thousand-Year Cloud Grass for a brew that can be steeped only once in an abbot's lifetime.
Pick cliff herbs until you find Thousand-Year Cloud Grass (rare), then bring it to Jue Yuan.
Jue Yuan steeps his brew. Sit with him.
The tea tastes like the first rain on hot stone. Jue Yuan says it tastes like ordinary tea, then laughs for a long time.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_rumput_taw: Every abbot here steeps one brew in his life: tea from Thousand-Year Cloud Grass. My master steeped his at ninety. I am eighty-seven, and the cliff pickers say that grass has grown very rare. Perhaps heaven wants me to learn patience. Or perhaps heaven wants you to pick it.
I'll look for it on the cliffs.
I did. She said the grass refuses to be picked by those who seek it. Then she said I'd have to pay double. That child will become a great merchant or a saint; I can't yet tell which.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_rumput_yao: Thousand-Year Cloud Grass? One in twenty pickings, if heaven is in a good mood. It grows in niches the morning mist touches. Raise your picker's rank, child; the high niches are more generous.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_rumput_sed: Ah. You know, I have practised steeping this tea in my head for sixty years, and now my hands shake like a young monk's. Sit. The first water is for the mountain, the second for my master, the third for us.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_jue_yuan_s: Welcome to the Cloud Monastery. Sit, if your legs still remember how. The young monks say the stairs are a trial; I say stairs are just stairs, and the trial is not complaining in front of the porters.
Tell me about the Cloud Bell.
What has been happening in town?
How does Gou Tie fare at the monastery?

The bell was cast from bronze carried up by three hundred porters, one handful each, over three pilgrimage seasons. That's why it never sounds the same twice. One hundred and eight strokes every noon in the Pilgrimage Season: one for each worry people carry to the summit. Rung quickly, because worries hate to wait.

Pilgrims gilded its roof tile by tile for two hundred years. Inside, the Bodhisattva sits on a white elephant with six tusks. If you arrive without flying, heaven leaves its blessing in your breath for seven days. If you fly, you only get the view. The view is nice too, mind you.
I have practised Dao Union for sixty years. Whenever someone challenges me, I offer them tea. Most forget why they were angry before the tea cools. The rest lose to the stairs before they get here.

He carries two sacks a day and grumbles three hundred times. Yesterday he fixed the storehouse roof unasked, then got angry when a young monk thanked him. Repentance rarely looks like a saint. Usually it looks like someone annoyed who keeps showing up.

The monastery gate is never locked, not even for those who carry gold. Sit. Shan Ling's basket is still in front of the gate; the monks dare not move it. If one day you wish to set something beside it, nobody will ask what.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_tie_suo_sa: The Iron Cable Car! Twenty years, one cable, zero riders dropped! One Spirit Stone up, free down, because going down is gravity's business and I don't pay gravity.
The monks call it the lazy road.
How is the new rope, Uncle?
How is the new rope, Uncle?
How is the new rope, Uncle?

With debt! The iron cable was forged in a smithing town three mountains away; I paid with promises, and I'm still paying those promises. The big wheel is from a pine felled by lightning. The monks called it a bad omen. I called it free timber.
Lazy! Their temple is full of rice and silk paper, and who carries it up? My car! The Abbot secretly rides it when his knee acts up. Don't say I told you.

The Ape Silk Rope sings when the wind passes! Truly, listen this evening: a low note, like a sleepy monk. Shan Ling rides the first cabin every morning, and the Old White Ape sits on the Middle Pylon watching us like a foreman. I toss it persimmons. It throws the peels back. That is friendship, on this mountain.

Strong. Stronger than the iron cable. But yesterday I found a single white hair caught in the big wheel, and since then I oil the rope at night, when nobody is watching. I don't know why. Maybe so the fibre knows someone cares for it, even if the way it was got... well. You know the way.

The car runs. Every morning the first cabin is full of Gou Tie's people's herb sacks; the pilgrims wait for the second. They pay, of course, exactly one Spirit Stone, smiling like owners. Twenty years I said my car was for tired legs. Now my car is for hungry purses.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_shan_ling_: If you want to pick on the cliffs, there are three rules: don't look down, don't carry food in your hand, and never trust a board that goes "creak" twice.
How do I rise as a picker?
Do you still visit the Old White Ape?
Shan Ling... about the White Ape.
I hear Gou Tie carries sacks now.

Monkeys! They're not thieves, they're tax collectors. A food tax. Hold a bun in your hand, and that bun belongs to the monkey state. A light tap, or toss fruit on the ground, and they drop their loot. I'm friends with them. Mostly.

Every picking earns points at the Herb Hall. Ten points, rank two; thirty, rank three; seventy, four; a hundred and fifty, five. High ranks open the high niches and a discount. Cloud Grass gives five points at once, if you're that lucky.

Wood herbs and wind herbs, sixty to three hundred years old, depending on how patient the cliff is. Sometimes, when the morning mist is generous, Thousand-Year Cloud Grass. I've only found it twice in my life. Twice!

Every full moon I bring it three persimmons and one red bean bun. It eats the persimmons and keeps the bun; I don't know who for. Yesterday it showed me a niche I had never seen. Twenty years of picking, and this cliff still keeps secrets. That's because of you, you know.

Don't. The rope is strong, the car runs, the town is happy. I pick, you pass. The monkeys don't come down to the plank walk any more, and nobody steals the bun from my hand. Turns out I miss being robbed.

I saw him on the four hundredth step, a rice sack on his back, and a little monkey sitting on the sack. He didn't shoo it away. I nearly fell off the cliff laughing. Maybe people can change after all. Slowly. Like a herb's age.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_lao_dan_sa: Want goods carried up? Two Spirit Stones a stack, there in about three minutes. Our porters aren't as fast as the car, but our porters never stall.
Send what's in my hand to the Golden Hall.
Send what's in my hand to the Cloud Monastery.
How long have you been a porter?
Is Gou Tie a good porter?
Fifty-two years. A thousand steps, twice a day, except the day I married and the day my wife died. People say my legs are iron. Not iron. Just a habit that doesn't know how to stop.

Good shoulders, bad breath. The first week he threw up on the third landing. The second week on the sixth. This week he reached the top and still had wind to curse. His grandfather was a porter in the same crew as me. I've never told him. Not yet.

Porters from the next mountain say a man with an iron claw offered gold for their cliffs. Their headman offered him tea and showed him the road home. News climbs stairs fast, friend. Faster than porters.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_jing_yue_s: Leave your shoes on the terrace, lower your voice inside the hall. This summit hears everything, especially what we think in secret.
When does the Buddha's Light appear?
Who is the statue on the elephant?

Register at the Foot Temple, light incense at the nine landings, reach this place before the day ends, without flying and without the car. For seven days after, your meditation on this terrace runs deeper, and anywhere your breath is a little clearer. Once every seven days. Heaven dislikes being bought in bulk.

On clear dawns, when the clouds below lie flat as cloth, a rainbow ring sometimes appears with your shadow at its heart. Stand on the viewing terrace and be still for ten breaths. People once leapt into it, thinking it the road to paradise. Do not leap.

Samantabhadra, the Bodhisattva of Great Practice. His elephant has six tusks: the six senses tamed. The statue is white stone, carved by four generations of carvers. The third got the elephant's left ear wrong, and the fourth did not dare fix it.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_yao_po_sap: Herbs, herbs, herbs! Bring them here, child, let Granny weigh their age. Appraisal is free. Advice is free too, but it usually costs more in the end.
How do you judge a herb's age?
Why have herb prices gone up, Granny?

Look at the root joints, smell the sap, listen to it snap. A hundred-year herb sounds like a twig; a three-hundred-year herb sounds like an old man coughing. This hall buys at half value, because we must dry them and feed the cat.
Fifteen Spirit Stones, single use. Tie it at your waist before picking: if you fall from this town's cliffs, it catches you once and snaps. Cheaper than a coffin, and cheaper still than a physician.

Because a man with an iron hand stands beside my scale every morning and nods or shakes his head. A fifth for him, child. Young pickers now climb higher and more recklessly for the same pay. Two fell this month. The Climbing Ropes are sold out. Granny is not happy to sell them.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_gou_kuli.m: Don't look at me like that. Yes, Iron Claw carries sacks. Twice a day. Lao Dan says in ten years I'll stop hating the stairs. I say five.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_gou_kuli.t: Sleeping soundly is strange. I used to count gold until morning. Now I count steps and fall asleep around the three hundredth.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_titipan_bi: There are parcels in your name, carried up by a porter this morning. The monastery kept them well; the monastery cat only sniffed them.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_titipan_au: Your parcels have arrived at the Golden Hall. The porter sang all the way up; his voice was awful, but your goods are whole.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_peziarah.m: Amitabha. Are you climbing too? My legs are not young, but my heart still wants to see that golden roof once more.
May you reach the summit safely.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_peziarah.n: Three steps, one prostration, if you want humility. One step, one breath, if you want to arrive. And hide your buns from the monkeys. That's not the Buddha's teaching, that's experience.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_kuli.mulai: Step aside a little, friend, load coming through! ... Hah. A hundred steps to the landing, then nine hundred more. Porters count down; pilgrims count up. That's why pilgrims tire faster.
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_biksu.mula: Amitabha. If you came on pilgrimage, register at the Foot Temple. If you came to run from something, these stairs take runaways too; they usually stop running at the fifth landing.
What do the monks do all day?
kultivator.cerita.tema_gunung_biksu.hari: The dawn bell, the wooden fish, porridge, sweeping leaves that never run out, a silent lunch, the Abbot's lecture, evening prayers, night meditation. Then tomorrow the leaves fall again. That is the teaching.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_gunung_ziar: The Pilgrimage Season has begun at the Mountain Town. They say the line of incense on the stairs can be seen from three valleys.
The stalls of the Pilgrims' Market doubled their incense and bamboo staffs. The Cloud Bell rings every noon.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_gunung_caha: This morning a rainbow ring stood on the clouds of the Golden Summit. All the monks bowed down.
A pilgrim says he saw his own shadow inside the Buddha's Light, and the shadow smiled.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_gunung_long: A rockslide at the Mountain Town! The plank walk is chained shut; stay off the cliffs while it rains.
A stone as big as a buffalo rolled down the upper stairs last night. Lucky the porters were asleep.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_gunung_mace: Uncle Tie Suo's cable car stalled above the gorge. He swears it isn't the cable's fault.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_gunung_tali: %s fitted a new cable to the Mountain Town's cable car. The Cloud Bell rang for them.
They say the cable car's new rope was spun by a white ape. %s brought it down from the cliff.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_gunung_ibu: The haughty scholar at the Foot Temple finally lit incense for his mother. %s climbed for him.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_gunung_kuli: %s carried three loads all the way to the Golden Hall without flying. Lao Dan says still not fast enough.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_gunung_kera: The Mountain Town monkeys lost five prizes because of %s. They are plotting revenge.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_gunung_rump: Abbot Jue Yuan finally steeped his Thousand-Year Cloud Grass tea. %s picked it.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_gunung_gou_: Gou Tie the Iron Claw now hauls sacks for the monastery. Some say he whistles on the stairs.
Gou Tie was driven out of the Mountain Town. The cliff pickers feasted on vegetable buns.
Herb prices at the Mountain Town rose by a fifth. People whisper that Gou Tie bought someone.
The young monks are betting how long the Iron Claw lasts as a porter. Lao Dan bet a lifetime, and he has never lost a bet.
The last of Gou Tie's spirit snares were burned in the Herb Hall yard. The smoke smelled of pine sap, and the monkeys watched from the roof.
Shan Ling left the Mountain Town before dawn. Her basket was left at the Cloud Monastery gate, and no monk dares move it.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_gunung_umum: The cable car is fast, sure, but porters never stall above a gorge.
My knees creak at every landing. Perhaps that's how they pray.
The monkeys at the fifth landing are the worst. They go after lit incense.
I came from the harbour town. The sea is not this high, but it is more patient.
The leaves in the monastery yard never run out. The Abbot says that's good for us.
The Cloud Bell sounds clearest in thick mist. Strange, but true.
The third niche from the top is most generous after rain.
Never pick with a bun in your left hand. The monkeys wait for that.
The great wheel needs oil again. Tie Suo says it's older than his wife, and more faithful.
Thunderstorm? The car stops. That's the one rule Tie Suo never breaks.
The scholar at the Foot Temple knows three hundred poems by heart, but has never reached the second landing without sitting down.
The Old White Ape only comes down when the mist is waist-high. Whoever sees it, they say, won't fall from the cliff that year.
The red bean buns at the Foot Market taste best eaten on the fourth landing. Don't ask why; my grandmother said so.
The Sutra Library keeps one scroll that may not be opened before the hundred-and-eighth bell. Nobody knows why yet.
advancement.kultivator.tempat.tema_gunun: Receive the Blessing of Light during the Buddha's Light at the Golden Hall.
Complete the Pilgrimage of a Thousand Steps seven times.
Climb for Pei Wenzhi's mother and tell him about the summit.
Carry three porter's loads up without flying.
Win back five things the monkeys stole from the pilgrims.
Bring Thousand-Year Cloud Grass for the Abbot's brew.
Hand Gou Tie to the monastery to atone as a porter.
